title: Tech Note: Defensive Programming 101
author: Timothy Aaron Penner, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This is a timeless, still-directly-applicable defensive-coding checklist — checking array bounds, validating pointers before dereferencing, testing file/folder paths before use, and cleaning up named selections — that remains standard advice for 4D developers today, even in Project Mode/ORDA-based code, since the underlying classic-language commands referenced (Size of array, Test path name, CLEAR NAMED SELECTION) are all still current.
related_updates: All referenced commands (Size of array, Test path name, CLEAR NAMED SELECTION) remain current in modern 4D
General defensive-programming principles apply equally to newer class-based/ORDA code
